# Research objective

This project investigates genomic prediction using regularized artificial
neural networks. Its main objective is to determine whether L1 and L2 weight
penalties improve predictive generalization relative to an unregularized
neural network and a GBLUP-ADE genomic mixed model.

The study combines controlled simulation with real longitudinal
*Coffea arabica* phenotypic and genomic data.

# Scientific design

The simulated and real-data branches use the same general analytical
separation:

1. preparation of the analytical data;
2. definition of the validation design;
3. independent fitting of GBLUP-ADE and ANN models;
4. terminal comparison of predictions obtained on matched held-out
   individuals.

The real-data branch contains one additional stage because repeated field
observations must be converted into individual phenotypic targets before
genomic prediction.

# Simulated data

The simulated branch contains six genetic scenarios with known true genetic
values.

Observed phenotypes provide the response used for model fitting, while the
known true genetic values remain excluded from model development and provide
an independent target for predictive assessment.

GBLUP-ADE is compared with ANN-0, ANN-L1, ANN-L2, and ANN-L1+L2 under common
outer-assessment partitions.

# Real Coffea arabica data

The real-data branch begins with the complete longitudinal field dataset.

Phenotypic preparation and genomic prediction are deliberately separated.

## Phenotypic mixed model

`real_data_phenotype.Rmd` operates only on the longitudinal phenotypic data.

The module:

- describes the observations and experimental structure;
- organizes repeated measurements and model factors;
- fits the defined mixed model by REML with `sommer`;
- summarizes the estimated variance components;
- obtains one final genotypic BLUP per individual and trait.

These BLUPs form the phenotypic targets used by the genomic-prediction branch.

## Genotype and phenotype integration

`real_data_audit.Rmd` combines the phenotypic BLUPs with the canonical
`geno_real.rds` genotype object.

This stage defines the common set and order of individuals, performs genotype
quality control, prepares the marker representation used by the genomic
models, and creates the common analytical object consumed downstream.

The phenotypic mixed model is not refitted during this integration stage.

# Genomic-prediction models

Five model configurations are evaluated:

- GBLUP-ADE;
- ANN-0;
- ANN-L1;
- ANN-L2;
- ANN-L1+L2.

GBLUP-ADE and ANN fitting are implemented in separate modules and use the same
outer-assessment design.

ANN model selection is restricted to the corresponding outer-analysis sample.

# Interpretation boundaries

The simulated and real-data branches answer related but distinct predictive
questions.

For simulated data, true genetic values are known and can be used directly for
independent evaluation.

For real data, the response used for genomic prediction is an estimated
genotypic BLUP obtained from the phenotypic mixed model. Predictive results
therefore describe the ability of genomic models to recover these adjusted
phenotypic genetic signals within the represented population and validation
design.

Held-out genomic predictions are not interpreted as final breeding values from
a model fitted with all available responses.

# Reproducible research

The repository uses R, R Markdown, `workflowr`, and `renv`.

Each analytical module has a specific responsibility and consumes defined
outputs from the preceding stage rather than repeating upstream processing.

Source pages are stored under `analysis/`, canonical derived objects under
`output/`, and the rendered website under `docs/`. Package versions required
by the project are recorded in `renv.lock`.
